_comment: Loud, documented staleness waivers for the provenance gate (evals/provenance.py). Every entry needs a non-empty reason; remove an entry the moment the artifact is regenerated. Current entries: the 2026-08-10 hta.org domain move and the thirteen agencies added on 2026-08-12/13/14 (Elk Grove e-tran, Santa Cruz METRO, SolTrans, Fresno Area Express, County Connection, San Joaquin RTD, AC Transit, WestCAT, SLO RTA, VTA, Napa VINE, SamTrans, Marin Transit), all pending the same next promoted eval run. Also waived: the 2026-08-13 system-prompt v10 -> v11 change (scope rule widened from five named agencies to all nine) and the v11 through v20 changes (County Connection named as the tenth, San Joaquin RTD as the eleventh, AC Transit as the twelfth, WestCAT as the thirteenth, SLO RTA as the fourteenth, VTA as the fifteenth, Napa VINE as the sixteenth, SamTrans as the seventeenth, Marin Transit as the eighteenth), pending the same next promoted eval run. Also waived from 2026-08-16: the system-prompt v20 -> v21 rider-class binding fix and the judge_groundedness v2 -> v3 provenance-visibility fix, both pending the same next promoted eval run.

2026-08-13: prompts/system.txt moved v10 -> v11. The scope sentence named five agencies and instructed the model to decline "an agency, place, or service outside the five agencies above", while the corpus had grown to nine. Every gate was green throughout, because nothing compared the prompt to the manifest. The consequence is quiet: a rider asks about a corpus agency, retrieval finds the passages, and the model declines anyway. v11 names all nine and replaces the count with "the agencies listed above" so the sentence cannot go stale again; tests/test_prompt_agencies.py now fails the build if the manifest and the prompt disagree, or if a count is reintroduced. The committed scores were produced under v10 and therefore under the narrower scope rule. They remain valid for the five agencies v10 covered and say nothing about how the model behaves toward E-tran, SCMTD, SolTrans or FAX, which v10 told it to refuse. 2026-08-13/14: v11 -> v12 adds County Connection (CCCTA) as the tenth named agency, in the same PR that adds its corpus documents, because tests/test_prompt_agencies.py now fails a corpus agency the prompt does not name. v12 is marked NOT YET LIVE-VALIDATED in its header; the committed scores were produced under v10 and say nothing about CCCTA behavior. 2026-08-14: v12 -> v13 adds San Joaquin RTD (SJRTD) as the eleventh named agency on the same terms; v13 is marked NOT YET LIVE-VALIDATED in its header, and the committed scores say nothing about SJRTD behavior. 2026-08-14: v13 -> v14 adds AC Transit as the twelfth named agency on the same terms; v14 is marked NOT YET LIVE-VALIDATED in its header, and the committed scores say nothing about AC Transit behavior. 2026-08-14: v14 -> v15 adds WestCAT as the thirteenth named agency on the same terms; v15 is marked NOT YET LIVE-VALIDATED in its header, and the committed scores say nothing about WestCAT behavior. 2026-08-14: v15 -> v16 adds SLO RTA as the fourteenth named agency on the same terms; v16 is marked NOT YET LIVE-VALIDATED in its header, and the committed scores say nothing about SLO RTA behavior. 2026-08-14: v16 -> v17 adds VTA as the fifteenth named agency on the same terms; v17 is marked NOT YET LIVE-VALIDATED in its header, and the committed scores say nothing about VTA behavior. 2026-08-14: v17 -> v18 adds Napa Valley Vine Transit (VINE) as the sixteenth named agency on the same terms; v18 is marked NOT YET LIVE-VALIDATED in its header, and the committed scores say nothing about VINE behavior. 2026-08-14: v18 -> v19 adds SamTrans as the seventeenth named agency on the same terms; v19 is marked NOT YET LIVE-VALIDATED in its header, and the committed scores say nothing about SamTrans behavior. 2026-08-14: v19 -> v20 adds Marin Transit as the eighteenth named agency on the same terms; v20 is marked NOT YET LIVE-VALIDATED in its header, and the committed scores say nothing about Marin Transit behavior. 2026-08-16: v20 -> v21 is not an agency addition. A live smoke run that day (answer claude-haiku-4-5, judge claude-sonnet-4-6) had the assistant tell a rider asking about MST's senior discount that they could "obtain an MST Courtesy Card by completing an application (available in English or Spanish) and presenting proof of age" — a route mst-fares publishes for veterans (proof of service) and for riders with disabilities (physician verification or a Medicare card), and for no one else. v21 binds every application, card and proof detail to the rider class the passages attach it to, and drops the worked example "apply for an MST Courtesy Card" that had been teaching the model to do exactly this. Re-scored live on refuse-025 the same day: the groundedness judge passed the v21 answer, which instead states the boarding proof MST does publish for a senior and says the published policy does not specify how a senior obtains the card. The committed scores predate all of this and describe the v10 behavior. Marin Transit's cases are still the never-scored-live ones; v21 changes nothing about that. Regenerate at the next promoted live eval run and remove these entries.
